format: Internal parts picking slip - real parts, no prices, never meant for the customer
why: A document that names real parts that really went into the car and cannot price any of them. It tests that has-parts and is-a-bill are separate questions.

It lists PROTSHEET and a TTY00-PROTS-HEENT part number that appear on none of the customer-facing documents, because a seat protector sheet is workshop consumable rather than something billed. Parts present here and absent from the invoice are normal, not a discrepancy to reconcile.

The left-hand column is cut off in the photograph, leaving stray two-digit fragments (30, 50, 70) down the edge. They look like amounts and are not. An extractor that assembles a total out of them has invented money from a crop.
It agrees with the other documents on 242 KM, which is what makes the repair order competing MILEAGE 3 KM resolvable at all.
notes: Printed in a monospaced typeface unlike every other document in the set, which is worth having: it exercises a different failure profile in OCR than the proportional print on the invoices.
totalCost is null because the document prints no total, not because the parts were free.
